messages:
Alex: FYI ran overnight perf sweep and noticed a regression in the paged-flash prefetch codepath when using Triton kernels on SM90 vs CUDA fallback. p99 latency up ~15-20% on long-seq workloads. attaching quick diff of profiles.
Maya: can you drop the perf command you used and a tiny repro? want to try on a local SM80 box.
Alex: repro command: `./bench --model=gpt-j --seq=2048 --bs=8 --prefetch=64 --arch=sm90 --kernels=triton,auto`
Alex: perf summary (tokens/sec): triton-sm90: 1850 (baseline 2250 on cuda fallback), cuda-sm90: 2220, cuda-sm80: 2280. CI perf alert flagged it: +18% token latency regression for paged_prefetch.
PerfBot: CI Alert: benchmark/paged_prefetch-nightly — sm90/triton — p99 regression +18% vs baseline (yesterday). Link: https://ci.internal/runs/5821
Jiro: interesting. could be the kernel selector picking a flash-variant that assumes contiguous KV layout, but our paged KV prefetch introduces small gaps and leads to warp divergence. did you capture smem/warp stalls?
Alex: attached nvprof flame snippet — big stall at `flash_prefetch_kernel_v2` on sm90. also saw increased atomic contention in prefetch allocator.
Sasha: hypothesis: batching heuristic is creating suboptimal batch composition (mixing short and long sequences) so prefetch window is mis-sized. if the runtime batches by time-since-arrival it can accidentally create wide batches of short sequences which thrash the paged prefetch.
Maya: can we toggle `force_cuda_path=true` in the selector to confirm it's Triton kernel-specific? If CUDA path solves it we know it's selector->kernel impl interaction.
Alex: quick toggle test: `runtime.conf.set("kernels.paged_prefetch.selector.force_cuda_path", "1")` on the canary cluster — perf restored to ~2210 tokens/sec. so yes, CUDA path avoids the regression.
Jiro: OK that narrows it. next steps: (1) bisect the triton kernel variants (v1,v2,v3) for sm90, (2) add a selector feature that considers kv_fragmentation_ratio and batch_seq_variance, (3) tune prefetch window (try 16/32/128) to see sensitivity.
Alex: tried prefetch=32 and saw p99 drop back to +2% — so window size matters. set prefetch=32 in a canary profile and rerunning.
Sasha: can also update batching heuristic: prefer max_batch_size=8 for paged attention when seq>1024, and prefer latency-first scheduling (dynamic_batch_threshold=20ms) to avoid creating huge mixed batches.
Maya: +1. make a canary config: when arch==sm90 && kernels==triton && model.tag==paged_prefetch then override: prefetch=32, max_batch_size=8, force_cuda_fallback_on_regression=false (so we can collect more traces).
Alex: created canary (cfg id: canary/flash-prefetch-sm90-2258). rolling to 5% now. collecting tracelogs and nvprof dumps. will report back after 2 hours. :thumbsup:
Jiro: if canary still shows regression we should instrument kernel entry to log `kv_fragmentation_ratio` and `batch_seq_variance` so selector heuristic can be data-driven. hitting this earlier will let us avoid brittle hand-tuned thresholds.
Maya: thanks — saved my afternoon chasing a mysterious throughput dip. keep updates here.
PerfBot: Perf data note: canary/flash-prefetch-sm90-2258 started at 2258001300, initial 5% rollout metrics available in dashboard.
